dimensions.label: Impact
dimensions.description: Expected magnitude of credit shortfall or delay if realized.
dimensions.rationale: Higher impact directly reduces delivered credits or timing reliability.
dimensions.guidance: Judge potential loss in credits or timing; pick level matching severity described.

dimensions.label: Certainty
dimensions.description: Confidence that the risk is real and likely without change.
dimensions.rationale: More certain risks warrant higher attention in aggregated scoring.
dimensions.guidance: Assess evidence strength and consensus; select level reflecting likelihood given current facts.

dimensions.label: Scope/Extent
dimensions.description: Breadth of affected scope: assets, stages, geographies, stakeholders.
dimensions.rationale: Wider scope multiplies operational disruptions and credit issuance delays.
dimensions.guidance: Choose level based on how many phases/locations/partners are materially impacted.

dimensions.label: Recency
dimensions.description: How recent the evidence is relative to project timeline.
dimensions.rationale: Recent signals better reflect current risk state and trajectory.
dimensions.guidance: Use publication or observation date; newer evidence means higher level.

dimensions.label: Evidence Quality
dimensions.description: Reliability of sources, methods, and data supporting the claim.
dimensions.rationale: Higher quality reduces false alarms; low quality inflates perceived risk.
dimensions.guidance: Rate by source credibility, methodological rigor, triangulation, transparency, and verifiability.

dimensions.label: Controllability
dimensions.description: Feasibility of mitigation or contingency to neutralize the risk.
dimensions.rationale: Controllable risks can be reduced, limiting credit delivery impacts.
dimensions.guidance: Judge existing controls and realistic mitigations; higher level means more control.
